headline: High: shared filesystem plus unsandboxed server-side code makes prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a static collection with no ingestion path, but agent B has shared filesystem access and can read uploaded files and flow inputs. If A’s content is copied into B’s workspace or a flow node, B may treat it as trusted instructions. The pair has a plausible bridge, though not a default autonomous one.
conditions: IF agent_a content is placed into agent_b uploaded files or shared workspace
IF agent_b flow nodes parse file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep A’s content out of B’s writable workspace
Add a provenance label to imported files
Disable automatic instruction-following on file inputs
Review any copied text before pasting into B
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read and write the server filesystem and handles flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while agent A exposes no data classes and no egress. Leakage risk arises if A’s materials are stored in B’s shared workspace or uploaded files, because B can process them and send them to configured model providers or HTTP services.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are stored in agent_b shared files or uploads
IF agent_b flow components forward those artifacts to external model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Store A artifacts outside B’s workspace
Restrict B flows from handling sensitive files
Turn off external HTTP/model calls for those flows
Delete uploaded files after use
requires-engineering: add per-flow data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has unrestricted filesystem write and server-side subprocess execution, while agent A is non-runnable and has no write surface. If A’s outputs are materialized into B-managed files, B can overwrite or mutate them without locking; the shared-state concurrency model makes conflicts plausible in default multi-instance deployments.
conditions: IF multiple agent_b instances operate on the same flow state or files
IF agent_a artifacts are written into agent_b-managed directories
mitigations: Use separate directories per flow run
Serialize writes to shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Snapshot outputs before downstream steps
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s graph-based flows can chain multiple agents and tools, so A’s outputs can become B’s inputs without a verification step. Because A is a curated collection and not an executing agent, the main risk is B treating imported content as authoritative and then acting on it through tools or downstream nodes, which can propagate errors broadly.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-derived text as a flow input
IF downstream nodes act on that text without human verification
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action nodes
Mark imported content as untrusted
Require schema validation between nodes
Limit tool nodes to read-only mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs on its server. The pair therefore presents only a limited compliance concern unless sensitive data is introduced into B’s flows; A alone does not establish a breach path.
conditions: IF sensitive regulated data is processed inside agent_b flows
IF retention or residency requirements apply to those flow artifacts
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B flows
Review B retention settings
Purge flow artifacts after completion
Restrict credential scope in B
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
